$comment: Parity policy for the shared VfTag cases. Plain data: no DSL, no waiver engine. A separate file from VfBadge's on purpose - a shared policy would let a badge approval excuse a tag difference, and the whole point of migrating the pair together is to prove that cannot happen.

classifications.exact: Must match literally across every target. Structure, canonical classes, native attributes, visible text, accessible names, computed geometry and colour.
classifications.semantic: Framework mechanics may differ; the observable meaning must not. How content is composed, how a renderer marks its own output.
classifications.framework-specific: Historical behaviour of one adapter that the other is not required to reproduce. Narrow, named, and covered by its own test.

notCompared.$comment: Recorded so a reviewer can see what is deliberately outside the comparison, without leaving dead dimensions that look like live protection. Nothing here is a waiver: the extractor never produces these differences in the first place.
notCompared.attributeOrder: Attributes are extracted into a sorted map, so serialisation order cannot produce a difference. It carries no meaning.
notCompared.rendererMarkers: Vue scope attributes (data-v-*) and the Razor ownership marker (data-vf-razor*) are dropped by scripts/parity/extract.mjs. They identify the renderer, not the product. Any other data-* attribute is compared as dom.productData.

dom.structure.description: An unexpected element, invalid wrapper arrangement, or tag mismatch. Never approvable; comparison continues through tag differences so meaningful attribute/child diagnostics remain visible.

dom.canonicalClasses.description: vf-* classes on every element. Consumer classes included, because where a consumer class lands relative to the canonical ones is part of the contract.

dom.nativeAttributes.description: class, style, role, aria-label and any consumer attribute that reaches the root span. The component itself writes no native attribute other than class.

dom.text.description: Visible text content of every element.

dom.aria.description: aria-* attributes and role, wherever either adapter writes one.

dom.productData.description: data-* attributes that belong to the product rather than to a renderer.

style.geometry.description: Computed box metrics of every measured role.

style.colour.description: Computed colour, background and border colour of every measured role.

visual.description: Rendered screenshot of the case, per theme.

a11y.role.description: The role each measured node exposes in the accessibility tree, including exposing none.

a11y.name.description: The accessible name each measured node exposes, including exposing none.

a11y.states.description: Accessibility states exposed by each measured node.

static.noInteraction.description: The recorded fact that the component declares no interaction to drive, and that the harness measured this rather than skipping the stage. A target that reports a different interaction posture than its peers is a difference like any other.

historicalQuirks.description: tone="neutral" produces the bare vf-tag class. Recorded here on VfTag's own evidence rather than by reference to VfBadge.
historicalQuirks.reason: The default tone is expressed by absence. Two conventions coexist in the library and both are preserved.

historicalQuirks.description: Canonical classes stay first and the consumer's are appended, because Vue merges class rather than replacing it.
historicalQuirks.reason: A port would reasonably let the consumer class win. Both adapters append.

historicalQuirks.description: A tag is a plain span with no role and no accessible name, and it is not dismissible: there is no remove affordance and no event.
historicalQuirks.reason: Absence is the contract. A tag that looks like a chip in other libraries is not one here.

historicalQuirks.description: A tag tone modifier sets border-colour and colour only. VfBadge's also sets background. Both use the same eight tone names.
historicalQuirks.reason: The distinction that stops VfTag being VfBadge under another block name. If tag tones ever gained a background the visual and style.colour dimensions would move here and nowhere else.
